definitions.reliability: Reliability is how complete, fresh, internally consistent and stable the information under this college projection is (lib/cfb_reliability.js, docs/football-reliability.md). It is a 0-100 score, not a probability, not the chance the projection is right, and not a betting signal.
definitions.data_check: The NFL model publishes no reliability score. This is the engine’s own input check: both starting quarterbacks named, enough games of team history, and no missing feature.
definitions.win_prob: EdgeDesk’s modelled probability that each team wins the game outright, from the engine’s own margin distribution. It is not a market-implied probability.
definitions.fair_ml: The model moneyline restates EdgeDesk’s win probability as American odds with no margin. It is a mathematical expression of a modelled probability, not a price any sportsbook is offering.
definitions.fair_spread: The point spread at which EdgeDesk’s projection has the two sides even: the projected margin, stated for the favourite and shown at the nearest half point (PK at zero). The unrounded margin is in the details, and every comparison uses it.
definitions.fair_total: EdgeDesk’s projected combined points, shown at the nearest half point. The unrounded total is in the details, and every comparison uses it.
definitions.projected_score: Each team’s projected points, rounded to whole points. The decimal expected points in the details split the unrounded total by the unrounded margin; the fair spread and total are rounded from those, not from the whole-number scores, so they can differ by a point.
definitions.key_number: A note when the model’s line and the market’s line sit on opposite sides of a key football margin (3 or 7), or one lands exactly on it. It describes the two lines only and changes no probability; how often games land on a margin differs between the NFL and college football.
definitions.range80: Eight in ten games like this one finish inside this margin range, read off the engine’s own distribution.
